component.name: OmniMem
component.summary: Self-hosted semantic memory for AI agents

description.p: OmniMem is a memory for your AI agents that you run yourself. Claude, Codex, Mistral Vibe, Kiro, OpenCode and anything else that speaks MCP can keep what they learn as they work and find it again in the next session, the next project or a different tool altogether. Decisions, bug fixes, gotchas, preferences and the approaches that didn't work all go into one file on your own machine.

Memories are searched by meaning rather than by keyword, using a small embedding model that runs locally. There's no account to make, and nothing leaves your computer unless you add a Claude API key for the optional extras.

ul.li: Recalls memories by meaning, so a question finds the answer even when it's worded differently
Keeps a graveyard of abandoned approaches, and warns an agent before it suggests one again
Briefs an agent at the start of a session with what the project already knows
Tracks when each memory was true and whether you trust it, so stale or disputed ones don't crowd out the rest
Reads your RSS feeds into a knowledge store, keeping each article's licence
Compiles what a project has learnt into skills, written only once you accept them
Backs up and restores your memories, including stores from OmniMem 6

description.p: OmniMem lives in the tray. Its menu shows whether the server is running, copies the MCP address to give to your agent, and opens the settings panel in your browser, already signed in. The panel is where you browse, search and edit memories, settle contradictions, accept skills, look after feeds and backups, and change settings.
The Flatpak's sandbox keeps OmniMem out of other apps' settings, so you add it to your agent yourself with the copied address. The guides at omnimem.org show how for each one.
The tray icon needs a desktop that shows tray icons. On GNOME that means the AppIndicator extension; without it OmniMem opens the settings panel instead and says so.

description.p: Every memory now says when it was true and when OmniMem believed it, and suppressed topics stay out of the briefing and the dead-end warnings. The store moves to a new schema on first start, so make a backup first.
A contradiction whose other memory no longer exists can be cleared.
The contradiction scan sees new memories on a full store, a forget takes the recall log entries that found the memory, and a person can settle a contradiction no scan linked.
OmniMem records whether it believes a memory, not only whether it shows it: each memory has a trust, and recall, the briefing and skill compiles act on it.
